name: Ungnadia

project_scope.note: Single-species genus study lesson uses identified neighboring taxa as references, not learner-approved new species. No new canonical species or nativity changes.

genus_recognition.look_here_first: Mexican buckeye is NOT a true Aesculus buckeye. Look at ALTERNATE pinnately compound leaves and a distinct woody THREE-LOBED CAPSULE that splits to reveal large glossy dark seeds. Rose-pink flowers appear early in spring.
genus_recognition.source_order: habit → leaf/stem architecture → flower structure → fruit/seed → specialist comparison

morphological_comparison_matrix.Ungnadia speciosa: alternate pinnately compound, several serrate leaflets and terminal leaflet
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Aesculus and Acer usually opposite leaves; Sapindus alternate pinnately compound too

morphological_comparison_matrix.Ungnadia speciosa: several leaflet pairs along central rachis, one tip leaflet
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Aesculus palmately compound with leaflets radiating from ONE point

morphological_comparison_matrix.Ungnadia speciosa: pink showy blooms often before full foliage
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Aesculus pavia also red pink flowers, so flowers alone not enough
Sapindus fruits round translucent fleshy drupes; Acer paired winged samaras

morphological_comparison_matrix.Ungnadia speciosa: large shiny very dark seeds in opened capsule
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Aesculus seeds large but leaves/fruit differ; Sapindus typically one round black seed per drupe

morphological_comparison_matrix.Ungnadia speciosa: deciduous small tree or multi-stem shrub of limestone/woodland regions
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Sapindus taller tree, Acer negundo riparian with V paired samaras

visual_id_sequence: 1. Inspect entire plant habit and growth form.
2. Zoom to stem node and complete mature leaf with ruler.
3. Inspect close flower and reproductive parts, labeling all structures rather than flower color alone.
4. Confirm mature fruit architecture with macro and seed view.
5. Compare the nearest confuser against matched structural photos; keep ambiguous IDs at genus.

diagnostic_photo_requirements.show: twig with alternate leaf attachment and rachis with cm ruler
opened 3-chamber fruit with dark seeds, labels + scale
flower cluster and early leaf emergence
Sapindus berry vs Ungnadia dry capsule vs Acer paired samara
seed exterior, fruit valve and internal partition detail
